test_title: PYST 32: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Inter-State Council is constituted under which Article?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 263**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 263** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to facilitate coordination between the states and the Union government.
 
• The **Inter-State Council** is constituted by the President if it appears to him that public interest would be served by its establishment.
 
• The council is meant to inquire into and advise upon disputes between states, investigate and discuss subjects of common interest, and make recommendations for better coordination of policy and action. *Hence, Article 263 is correct.*
 
• The council plays a significant role in fostering cooperative federalism in India by serving as a platform for discussion between the Union and state governments.
 
• The **Inter-State Council** is not a permanent body and is constituted as and when required. The President has the discretion to determine its composition, nature of duties, and procedure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Articles mentioned in the options:**

 
 
• **Article 368:** This article deals with the procedure for the **amendment of the Constitution**. It does not deal with the creation of the Inter-State Council. This makes it an incorrect option.
 
• **Article 280:** It deals with the establishment of the **Finance Commission** by the President. The Finance Commission is responsible for making recommendations on the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Article 346:** This article pertains to the official language for communication between states and between a state and the Union. It has no relevance to the Inter-State Council. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Inter-State Council:**
 
 
• The council aims to promote a spirit of cooperative federalism by resolving disputes and ensuring collaboration between different levels of government in India.
 
• It is an **important institution** for discussing policies and ensuring uniformity in their implementation across states.
 
 
 
• **Examples of its use:**
 
 
• The Inter-State Council has been utilized to discuss critical issues such as the sharing of river waters, disaster management, and other inter-state disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The idea of establishing an Inter-State Council was first recommended by the **Sarkaria Commission**, which was set up in **1983** to review the existing Center-State relations and recommend changes.
 
• The council was first constituted in **1990** under the chairmanship of the then Prime Minister **Vishwanath Pratap Singh**.
 
 
 
• **Composition:**
 
 
• The council comprises the **Prime Minister** as the Chairperson, Chief Ministers of all states, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, and administrators of UTs without legislatures.
 
• Additionally, Union Cabinet Ministers in charge of home affairs and other ministers nominated by the Prime Minister are also members.
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• It inquires into and advises upon disputes between states and the Union, investigates and discusses matters of common interest, and makes recommendations for better coordination of policy and action.
